headline: SILVER CRASHES 10.6%, GOLD FALLS TO $4,564 AS HOT APRIL CPI KILLS RATE-CUT BETS
snippet: April CPI came in at 3.8% — above forecasts — triggering a synchronized selloff across metals on May 15. Gold fell 1.83% to $4,564/oz while silver plunged 10.6% to $77.52, its worst single-day drop in months. Markets have now fully priced out Fed rate cuts for 2026, with some traders pricing in a December hike. Copper fell 5.12% the same session.

headline: SILVER ENTERS 6TH STRAIGHT SUPPLY DEFICIT YEAR; CUMULATIVE SHORTFALL TO REACH 866M OZ BY YEAR-END
snippet: Despite the price whipsaw, silver is structurally in deficit for a sixth consecutive year. The cumulative shortfall is projected to reach 866 million oz by end-2026, driven by explosive demand from solar panels, EVs, AI data centres, and emerging tech. Silver hit an intraday high of $89.33 on industrial demand last week before the CPI-driven selloff pulled it back below $78. Platinum is also showing strength, decoupling from gold.

headline: LI-FT POWER HITS 26M AT 1.29% Li2O AT BIG EAST PEGMATITE — YELLOWKNIFE LITHIUM PROJECT, NWT
snippet: Li-FT Power (TSX-V: LIFT) reported 26m at 1.29% Li2O from its 2026 winter program at Yellowknife, including 17m at 1.65% Li2O, at the BIG East pegmatite complex. Results confirm the deposit's southern extent is open at depth and along strike. The project hosts 50.4Mt at 1.00% Li2O in inferred resources — one of the largest hard-rock spodumene deposits in North America.

headline: GOLD DOWN 16% FROM JANUARY HIGH BUT J.P. MORGAN, WORLD BANK STILL TARGET $5,000
snippet: Gold has corrected 16% from its $5,589 January all-time high to around $4,564, yet institutional forecasters haven't blinked. J.P. Morgan projects $5,000 by year-end, the World Bank's April Commodity Outlook projects a 42% surge for gold and silver, and central banks bought a net 244 tonnes in Q1 2026 — even as prices were near record highs. Published May 12, 2026.

headline: SILVER OUTLOOK: STOP CHASING THE NUMBER — WATCH THE GOLD-SILVER RATIO INSTEAD
snippet: After silver's round trip from its $121.64 January all-time high to below $78, GoldSilver.com argues the metal's dual nature — monetary and industrial — makes price-chasing dangerous in this environment. The gold-silver ratio's compression from 62:1 to 55:1 in a single week following the US-China tariff truce is the more reliable directional signal than spot price alone.

headline: COPPER TANKS 5% FROM RECORD HIGHS; ICSG WARNS OF 150,000-TONNE STRUCTURAL DEFICIT IN 2026
snippet: Copper fell 5.12% to $6.23/lb on May 15 as traders booked profits, but the structural picture remains tight. The International Copper Study Group projects a 150,000-tonne market deficit for 2026, citing Indonesia's Grasberg mine disruptions through Q2 and production growth slowing to just 0.9%. Copper is still up 36.9% year-over-year. ING forecasts a 600,000-tonne refined deficit.

headline: URANIUM SPOT SLIPS TO $86/LB IN METALS ROUT; UEC DROPS 6.4% ON HEAVY VOLUME MAY 16
snippet: Uranium spot fell to $85.95/lb on May 15 as the inflation-driven commodity selloff hit nuclear fuel markets. Uranium Energy Corp. (NYSE: UEC) saw 9.97M shares change hands on May 16 — above average — dropping 6.4% to $13.64. Despite short-term weakness, uranium is still up 20% year-over-year as tech giants sign SMR contracts and utilities extend reactor life.

headline: RARE EARTHS AMERICAS SURGES 26% ABOVE IPO PRICE ON NYSE AMERICAN DEBUT, TARGETS US HEAVY RARE EARTH SUPPLY
snippet: Rare Earths Americas (NYSE: REA) raised $63.3M in an oversubscribed IPO at $19/share and immediately surged 26% to $24+ on its NYSE American debut. The company is betting on its Shiloh heavy rare-earth district in Georgia, which could supply NdPr for U.S. defense and permanent magnet supply chains — and potentially reshape domestic rare-earth processing capacity.

headline: NdPr OXIDE PLUNGES 21% IN APRIL TO $99/KG; CHINA'S JUNE MINING QUOTA IS THE NEXT BIG TRIGGER
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium oxide fell 21% in April to $99.61/kg — the sharpest monthly decline since the Q1 rally — pulling neodymium and praseodymium individual oxides with it. Despite the drop, NdPr remains 88% above its January open and well above Western producers' cost bases including MP Materials and Lynas. All eyes are on China's mid-year MIIT mining quota announcement, expected in June.

headline: GOLDSEEK WEEKLY: GOLD, SILVER AND MINING STOCKS AWAITING NEXT CATALYST AFTER INFLATION SHOCK
snippet: GoldSeek's Issue #72 weekly roundup surveys the post-CPI landscape for precious metals and mining equities. With CLSA upgrading its 2026 gold target to $4,840 and UBS projecting $5,900 by year-end, analysts assess whether the pullback has created a tactical entry point for junior miners or whether sticky inflation will keep equities under pressure into Q3.

headline: LI-FT POWER AND WINSOME RESOURCES UPDATE TIMETABLE FOR CANADA-AUSTRALIA LITHIUM COMBINATION
snippet: Li-FT Power (TSX-V: LIFT) has updated the proposed timetable for its combination with ASX-listed Winsome Resources in a cross-border deal that would consolidate two significant hard-rock lithium exploration companies. LIFT's Yellowknife Lithium Project holds 50.4Mt at 1.00% Li2O — one of North America's largest spodumene deposits. The combined entity targets a stronger position ahead of expected lithium deficit conditions.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE BOOM LIFTS LITHIUM DEMAND OUTLOOK; MORGAN STANLEY SEES 80,000-TONNE DEFICIT IN 2026
snippet: A surge in grid-scale battery storage — particularly in China — has strengthened the demand outlook for lithium after years of oversupply misery. Morgan Stanley now forecasts an 80,000-tonne LCE deficit in 2026; UBS sees 22,000 tonnes short. China's power sector reforms drove stronger-than-expected lithium demand in H2 2025, setting up a cautiously optimistic 2026 outlook for hard-hit producers.
